hints: Square both non-negative modulus expressions to obtain an ordinary quadratic inequality.
Expand $(2x-1)^2<9(x+1)^2$ and find the two equality roots.
Test the intervals separated by those roots; retain the two exterior intervals and exclude the boundary values.
walkthrough:
Since both sides of the inequality $|2x - 1| < 3|x + 1|$ are non-negative, square both sides:
$$(|2x - 1|)^2 < (3|x + 1|)^2$$
$$(2x - 1)^2 < 9(x + 1)^2$$

Collect all terms on one side to form a 3-term quadratic inequality:
$$(9 - 4)x^2 + (18 - (-4))x + (9 - 1) > 0$$
$$5x^2 + 22x + 8 > 0$$

Solve the corresponding quadratic equation $5x^2 + 22x + 8 = 0$ by factorising:
$$(5x + 2)(x + 4) = 0$$
This gives the two critical values:
$$x = -4 \quad \text{and} \quad x = -\dfrac{2}{5}$$

Determine the solution set of the strict inequality $5x^2 + 22x + 8 > 0$:
Since the leading coefficient $5$ is positive, the quadratic is strictly positive outside the roots:
$$x < -4 \quad \text{or} \quad x > -\dfrac{2}{5}$$
